8829d551d5aef47e8e108773c49e191c8e0227f1.summary: Intel 471 blog post, published 4 May 2020, on version 2.2 of the REvil ransomware-as-a-service operation's malware. The update restores a registry Run-key persistence mechanism that version 2.1 had removed. It adds use of the Windows Restart Manager to end processes and services that hold files open before encryption, and a silent-mode option that skips termination of blacklisted processes and shadow copy deletion. The report notes that the same Restart Manager technique appears in SamSam and LockerGoga, and that stopping protected processes may cause undefined behaviour on victim systems.

88832209d51f193186daf5d026225be82513aefa.summary: Archived profile of the threat actor Deep Panda, also known as Shell Crew, APT 19 and other names. The report says the actor compromises high-tech sector companies, the U.S. defense industrial base, nongovernmental organizations and state and federal government entities for espionage. It is suspected of being behind breaches at Anthem, the U.S. Office of Personnel Management and United Airlines. China is listed as the suspected state sponsor and the United States as a suspected victim.

Covers builds from a November 2025 x86 prototype to ARM builds with three encryption layers, DNS-over-HTTPS C2 resolution, and ADB-based delivery to Android TV boxes from January 2026. Reports links to Aisuru and the CatDDoS derivative ecosystem. Law enforcement disrupted the operation on March 19, 2026, after which C2 capacity fell sharply and a smaller Ethereum Name Service fallback appeared.

881012ca3fd522f51e6cb92b15f40807b4072573.summary: Objective-See's Patrick Wardle analyses UpdateAgent, the second-stage macOS payload of the 3CX supply chain attack. The post attributes the campaign to North Korean actors, aka Lazarus Group, as cited by the author. The x86_64 binary is ad-hoc signed and not notarised. It forks, self-deletes, reads a 3CX config file and a victim identifier, and prepares a request to a remote server that was offline during analysis. The author suggests it mainly reports victim information. Detection with BlockBlock, DNSMonitor and LuLu is described.

8831939056d868d10d86da0d8dd9b37ee7518052.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group reports several threat actors exploiting CVE-2025-55182 (React2Shell), an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in React Server Components disclosed on Dec. 3, 2025. Activity includes China-nexus clusters deploying MINOCAT, SNOWLIGHT, HISONIC, COMPOOD and ANGRYREBEL.LINUX, plus financially motivated XMRig cryptomining. Iran-nexus exploitation is also noted. Vulnerable packages are React Server Components 19.0 to 19.2.0 used by React and Next.js. The report recommends patching and deploying a WAF rule as a temporary mitigation.
